feature: A border meets the fill and the edge cleanly
summary: A border now separates what is on either side of it completely. An inner border no longer lets a hairline of the fill show along its outside, and an outside border no longer lets a hairline of the background show along its inside.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to turn on: this is how every border draws now.

try.do: Draw a rectangle on a coloured background and give it a bright fill.
Set Corner Radius to about 20, so the corners are properly curved.
In Effects, add a Border, set Position to Inside and Width to 8, and pick a colour that contrasts with the fill (black on red is the clearest).
Zoom to 800% and look along the OUTSIDE of the border, especially round the corner. It should go background straight to border, with no trace of the fill.
Switch Position to Outside and look along the INSIDE of the border, again round the corner. It should go border straight to fill, with no trace of the background.
Switch Position to Centre and check both of its edges the same way.
Set the border's colour to something half transparent and check the fill still shows through the band.

evaluate: At 800%, does the corner of an inner border read as one clean line, or can you still find a warm pixel where the fill used to leak?
Does the outside of the shape still look smoothly curved, or has it gained a hard, stepped edge?
On an outside border, does the border look like it is sitting ON the shape rather than floating a hair off it?
Does a half transparent border still look like the fill is showing through it, rather than washing out?
Do borders on ovals look as clean as borders on rectangles, or is one noticeably worse?
rough: An OVAL with an outside border keeps a faint trace of the background round its diagonals: about twenty pixels at a twentieth of the background's strength, down from hundreds at three times that. An oval's border is drawn as a stroke ridden round the oval, because that is how the shape draws its own edge, and a stroke's inner boundary is not itself an oval. Filed as its own task.

Composing a border costs more than it did. On the standard 12 megapixel, 10 layer document an interactive edit went from 5.5ms to 6.4ms and a full render from 38ms to 37ms, both inside budget; the heaviest case in the suite, an edit inside a styled group of five, went from 36ms to 46ms. Confining the correction to the band itself instead of the whole layer would win most of that back; filed as its own task.

The before and after pictures here are renders magnified ten times, not screen captures: a one pixel seam is invisible at life size, which is the whole reason it took a magnified screenshot to report. The third shot IS a real screen capture from the probe, with an outside and an inside border on the same shape.
